Lost fifty percent on your stock? A fifty percent rise is the wrong fix.
Wait, what? My stock fell fifty. If it goes up fifty, I'm back, right?
Nope. You'd still be down twenty five percent.
Take a hundred rupees. It falls fifty percent. You're left with fifty.
Now it rises fifty percent. But fifty percent of fifty is just twenty five. So you reach seventy five. Not a hundred.
Then what does it really need?
A hundred percent. It has to double, just to get back.
Double? Is that only for big falls?
It gets worse as the fall gets bigger. Down ten, needs eleven. Down twenty, needs twenty five. Down thirty, needs forty three. Down eighty? Four hundred percent.
Has this happened to the whole market?
In March twenty twenty, Nifty fell about forty percent, from twelve thousand four thirty to seventy five eleven. To get back, it needed sixty five percent. It took until November.
So how do I protect myself?
Keep losses small. Decide your exit before you buy, and don't put too much in one stock. A small loss is easy to recover. A big one can take years.
Got it. Small losses, not big ones.
Save this before your next trade. And send it to the friend who says, my stock fell fifty percent.
